$comment: Production defaults from COMPOSITION.md. Starting points, not genre definitions: establish tempo and structure from the references first. Sections are 1-based bars; energy 0..1 drives which roles play (see composition partsForEnergy).

house.defining_idea: hook, riff, vocal or bass identity

deep_house.priority: Warm harmony, subtle movement, restrained transitions
deep_house.voicing: sevenths and ninths; parallel or voice-led; keep chords out of the sub register

melodic_techno.priority: Few strong parts, one recognisable motif, kick-locked mono bass with negative space, evolving timbre, long tension curves
melodic_techno.defining_idea: lead motif or arp with timbral evolution

sections.name: Intro
sections.note: DJ intro: kick, filtered texture, sparse top percussion

sections.name: Groove
sections.note: hats, clap, primary percussion

sections.name: Low End
sections.note: bass enters; first tonal cue

sections.name: Motif Tease
sections.note: partial lead or arp, heavily filtered

sections.name: Build
sections.note: more high-frequency information, delay/reverb movement

sections.name: Break
sections.note: kick removed; motif and harmony exposed; more spatial depth (4 to 6/10)

sections.name: Drop A
sections.note: kick + bass + the complete motif

sections.name: Drop A Variation
sections.note: percussion and counter detail; alter the motif ending

sections.name: Reset
sections.note: lead removed; change the timbral perspective

sections.name: Peak Build
sections.note: ride, brighter hats, widened upper layers; lead held back

sections.name: Final Peak
sections.note: full motif; strongest rhythmic and spectral density

sections.name: Outro
sections.note: melodic layers then bass removed, leaving DJ-friendly rhythm (6 to 2/10)

melodic_techno.source: MELODIC-TECHNO.md: 192-bar curve (six minutes at 128 BPM) and arrangement template; agent defaults, not measured from references

techno.voicing: pedal tones and drones; change upper intervals over a fixed bass

progressive_house.source: ERIC.md DJ-friendly progressive blueprint (Pryda-leaning mode): a controlled reveal - establish, hint, add, withdraw, expose, intensify, release, rebuild, peak, dissolve
progressive_house.priority: Groove, tonal identity, long-form development, automation, spatial depth, contrast - only then more layers
progressive_house.defining_idea: a small motif (2-5 notes) whose meaning changes through filter, register, delay and withholding

sections.name: Intro
sections.note: utility intro: kick, filtered percussion, a tiny hint of tonal material

sections.name: Groove
sections.note: groove identity: bass becomes clear, hats establish motion, filtered motif hint

sections.name: Development
sections.note: open the filter gradually; the chord/pluck cell appears

sections.name: Development b
sections.note: second harmonic layer, FX punctuation at 8/16-bar boundaries, more of the motif - not full brightness

sections.name: Main A
sections.note: first payoff: full kick/bass and main groove layers; the lead is not revealed yet

sections.name: Breakdown
sections.note: remove the low end, keep one tonal anchor, lengthen the reverb, expose the harmony

sections.name: Breakdown b
sections.note: a tiny original lead cell enters near the end of the breakdown

sections.name: Rebuild
sections.note: rhythm returns in stages; noise and risers support but are not the build; low end held back

sections.name: Main Peak
sections.note: strongest bass, full chord/pluck relationship, the lead, brighter percussion

sections.name: Outro
sections.note: remove the lead and emotional layers, simplify to groove, filters back to a DJ-friendly state

hypnotic_long_form.source: Measured from Underworld's Cowgirl (2014 remaster, 127 BPM): a 64-bar gradual build, a long plateau at near-constant level, one late breakdown and a final stretch. The energy curve is measured; the roles are a melodic techno reading of it, not the original's parts.
hypnotic_long_form.priority: One tonal centre held for minutes; development through the arpeggio's timbre, cycles and density rather than harmony
hypnotic_long_form.defining_idea: an arpeggio whose cycles drift against the bar while its filter opens across the build

sections.name: Intro
sections.note: kick, 3-against-4 rim, texture

sections.name: Build
sections.note: hats and the pedal bass pulse

sections.name: Build b
sections.note: the arpeggio enters, heavily filtered

sections.name: Build c
sections.note: clap and the 5-step tom polymeter; the filter keeps opening

sections.name: Plateau
sections.note: full groove with the open arpeggio; evolve it by automation, not parts

sections.name: Plateau b
sections.note: the counter-arpeggio interlocks on different cycle lengths

sections.name: Plateau c
sections.note: toms polymeter returns under both arpeggios

sections.name: Plateau d
sections.note: harmony finally arrives over the pedal (late colour)

sections.name: Breakdown
sections.note: kick and bass out; arpeggios and harmony exposed

sections.name: Final
sections.note: everything, strongest

sections.name: Outro
sections.note: back to rhythm for the DJ

tinlicker.source: TINLICKER.md long-form structure (section 20): intro, establishment, development, breakdown, rebuild, payoff with layers revealed after 8 bars, second development with a new counterline, outro that keeps the groove and drops the melodic focus
tinlicker.priority: Emotional chord movement, bass movement, kick/bass groove, one primary motif - then trajectory, atmosphere and detail
tinlicker.defining_idea: a 3-6 note motif and a 2-4 chord loop whose bass line, not chord complexity, carries the lift

sections.name: Intro
sections.note: groove first, DJ-friendly entry, restrained harmony

sections.name: Intro b
sections.note: the motif as a filtered ghost

sections.name: Establishment
sections.note: bass becomes clear, full drum identity, pluck/arp introduced

sections.name: Development
sections.note: harmony established, brighter timbre, added percussion, tension begins

sections.name: Breakdown
sections.note: kick and sub out; the harmony and motif exposed; it should still work with only pad, motif and texture

sections.name: Rebuild
sections.note: rhythmic clues return, rising filter, percussion acceleration - the kick stays out until the drop

sections.name: Drop
sections.note: kick and bass return decisively, the hook clear; supporting layers held back

sections.name: Drop b
sections.note: the held-back layers revealed after 8 bars

sections.name: Second Development
sections.note: variation, not copy/paste: a new counterline, a changed bass ending, different percussion

sections.name: Outro
sections.note: melodic focus removed, groove retained

sections.name: Outro b
sections.note: progressively simplify for the next record

hopkins_journey.source: JON_HOPKINS.md arrangement blueprint (section 18) as emotional states (section 11.1). Its timings are converted to bars at 126 BPM and rounded to the 8-bar grid; the document says bar lengths follow the musical need, so treat these as a trajectory, not a formula.
hopkins_journey.$dj_friendly: JON_HOPKINS.md opens with environment and closes with integration rather than DJ beat-only intros and outros, so the kickless intro/outro rule does not apply.
hopkins_journey.priority: Emotion, identity and trajectory before sound; transformation over surface imitation
hopkins_journey.defining_idea: one simple emotional seed carried for minutes while its source, space, density and damage keep changing

sections.name: Intro (orientation)
sections.note: environment / seed: texture and a fragment of the motif

sections.name: Build: pulse
sections.note: the pulse appears - ideally caused by something already present

sections.name: Build: hypnosis
sections.note: motif and bass establish hypnosis

sections.name: Build: rhythmic systems
sections.note: orbiting loops of different lengths accumulate

sections.name: Peak: pressure
sections.note: pressure, distortion, instability - comfort before discomfort

sections.name: Breakdown: rupture
sections.note: rupture or opening: negative space; the bass leaves

sections.name: Peak: expansion
sections.note: emotional melodic expansion

sections.name: Transformed return
sections.note: the opening material returns transformed

sections.name: Outro (integration)
sections.note: decompression and exit

groove.anchor: Keep the kick quantised until there is a musical reason not to.
groove.order: velocity variation before timing changes; bass only if it improves the drum/bass pocket

arrangement_rules.note: Change is not the same as adding a layer: subtract, filter, modulate. Reserve the fullest state for the real peaks.

palettes.natural_minor: Aeolian: i-VI-III-VII cyclic, i-VII-VI-VII hypnotic, i-iv-VII-III journey
palettes.dorian: Minor centre with a bright major sixth: i-IV exposes the colour; i-ii-IV-i moves gently
palettes.harmonic_minor: Raised seventh for a darker leading tone
palettes.phrygian: Flat second for a dark, tense techno colour
